about: What is known about each model that crucible could route a role to: ids per provider, price, speed, benchmark scores with their sources, the result of crucible's own calibration probes, and `fit`: the role it suits here. routing.json is the table the engine uses; this file is the evidence behind it. Regenerate with calibration/build_model_map.py after new research or a calibration.
caveats: Most benchmark numbers are vendor-reported or come from aggregators (see each score's source_type); compare models only within one benchmark and one scaffold.
The Artificial Analysis index and speed figures were read through an aggregator page; effort labels on that page were partly inferred.
Anthropic does not publish how much of a subscription limit each model draws. The weights in routing.json follow API prices, which is a guess.
Calibration probes are a floor test (12 small tasks): every model passed nearly all of them, so they show speed, cost and robustness, not which strong model is better.

system_one_models.definition: TypeSafe's term (after Kahneman): non-autoregressive models that read 'state' plus predefined questions and return typed probabilistic decisions (choice, score, noul=yes/no probability, box in 1.14) in one parallel pass; no free text. Trained with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD).
system_one_models.who_is_typesafe: TypeSafe AI, founded by Diogo Almeida (ex-OpenAI, helped build instruction-following/ChatGPT research), two years stealth, Jev announced 2026-09-15 (primary: typesafe.ai blog).

Jev.speed: vendor: 70-500 ms end-to-end; Reddit snippet ~150 ms
Jev.context: 64k per request/32k per question default; 262k with long-context header; Runware lists 262,144
Jev.also_on: Runware typesafe:jev@1.14; Vercel AI Gateway (Runware says ~13% of paid teams used it in 24h)
Jev.vendor_claims: 193.6x faster, 444.6x cheaper than LLM baselines on TypeSafe's own workflow evals, reference = average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1; 'cannot hallucinate' means cannot emit invalid type, not cannot be wrong
independent: Runware engineer: synthetic phishing, asked directly Jev 62.6% vs Claude Haiku 4.5 81.3%; decomposed into 5 signals + code 95%; domain rules 91.8%

arXiv 2609.33401 (TraceStone/NTU): Jev, Laya, Decider, Bespoke Nimble on agent security decisions; good average accuracy/calibration hides confident misses on some attack groups; second judge repeats errors

Laya.what: Open-weight (Apache 2.0) decision model by Convai Innovations, NOT TypeSafe's. English checkpoint ModernBERT-large + decision head; multilingual mmBERT; Jev-compatible API with choice/score/noul.
Laya.speed: vendor: 39.5 ms (English) and 32.8 ms (multilingual) per question on Tesla T4; 10 questions 158.6/72.3 ms
Laya.accuracy: vendor synthetic benchmark (2000 decisions): specialized checkpoint 76.6%; general English checkpoint 36.2% vs 46.1% majority baseline
Laya.limits: 512-token context default (1024 multilingual/specialized); ~20 options advised max; probabilities can be overconfident
Laya.controversy: Reddit/Medium/YouTube snippets discuss whether Jev derives from Laya or vice versa; unresolved, not opened
Laya.other_names: Decider and Bespoke Nimble are other System One-style models named in the arXiv paper; Berget AI offers Laya in Sweden

system_one_models.fit: Both: routing, triage, scoring, judge/guardrail slots where answers are bounded. Not general reasoning. Sanz's advice: decompose into atomic questions, combine in code, test against small LLM with structured output and plain rules, calibrate thresholds.

plans.Max: $100/mo, 'five times the Pro plan's usage every five hours and every week'
plans.Max_20x_or_Ultra: $200/mo; Anthropic help center now also lists an 'Ultra' plan; third-party pages call $200 tier Max 20x

metering: 5-hour limit plus a weekly limit across all models (primary)

separate weekly meter for Fable models; on Max/Ultra Fable can use up to 50% of weekly limit, then usage credits or switch model; draws from the same weekly pool and 'use them faster than other Claude models' (primary)
Claude on web/desktop/mobile, Claude Code and Cowork share limits (userightai, secondary)
Anthropic publishes multipliers not message counts; weekly limits reset at an account-specific time
claude.per_model_cost_against_limit: No official per-model rates. SemiAnalysis (Oct 5 2026, secondary, paywalled charts): each (model, token type) consumes different credits; Anthropic reduces API-equivalent value for premium models: small drop Sonnet 5.5 -> Opus 5.5, large drop at Fable 5.1; Opus 5.5 token limits raised ~20% on Max and ~50% on Pro after price cut. Haiku 5.5 metering not found.
claude.monthly_api_credits: Max $100/$200 per month API credits since 2026-10-07, claimed in Console, separate from chat/Code allowance (userightai, secondary; Anthropic help text confirms credits exist)

facts: Plus $20; Codex included; est. 15-160 local messages/5h on GPT-6.1 Sol (aibusinessweekly snippet); kipt.me snippet: Plus per-5h ranges Astra 5-45, 6.1 Sol 15-160, Luna 350-3000

Per OpenAI help center (primary, opened): from December Plus, Pro, Business allowances are shared across ChatGPT and Codex, measured in tokens, heavier models use more; instant chat does not draw usage
SemiAnalysis: OpenAI halved $200 Pro limits in late Sep 2026 and added $500 tier; Pro plans have no 5-hour limit

value_vs_api.semianalysis_oct5_2026: secondary, paywalled: $200 Claude plan ~ $11,726 of Opus 5.5 agentic API-equivalent per month (via explainx/tokenpost snippets); ChatGPT Pro $200 ~ $2,084 (explainx snippet); Opus 5.5 on Claude ~4-5x OpenAI value. Opened article text: $200 Anthropic plan has 50% left after $2,485 of Fable 5.1; OpenAI equivalent exhausted after $2,897 of Astra. Anthropic tiers give equal per-dollar value across Pro/Max.
other: medium snippet: $200 Max 20x = $2,800-$7,470 API at standard rates depending on use
atticusli.com snippet: one user's real usage API-equivalent $7,814 for Jul 1-20 2026
GitHub issue anthropics/claude-code#108599 (Nov 9): users report effective limits ~1/3 lower since ~Oct 30
value_vs_api.caveat: For a $100 plan, scale linearly: Anthropic says same per-dollar value across tiers (SemiAnalysis), so Max $100 would be roughly half of the $200 figure; inferred.
